headline: Passengers stranded as bus services from Rajshahi suspended on all routes
summary: A dispute between bus owners and workers in Rajshahi and Natore districts has halted all inter-district bus services, including those to Dhaka.
details: Inter-district bus services from Rajshahi to Dhaka and other destinations were suspended on Saturday morning, leaving hundreds of passengers stranded at the terminal.
// a direct bus service from Rajshahi to Darshana was recently launched, but it was stopped by motor workers in Natore.
// This incident sparked a conflict between bus owners and workers of the two districts, which had been escalating for several days.
// Prior to the total suspension, several buses from both districts had been detained by opposing groups.
// The sudden halt in services has caused significant hardship for passengers arriving at the Rajshahi bus terminal.
// Discussions are currently underway between the relevant parties to resolve the dispute and resume normal operations.

headline_marked: Jamaat-led alliance [[begins Dhaka-Chattogram long march]] for people's rights
headline: Jamaat-led alliance begins Dhaka-Chattogram long march for people's rights
summary: The 11-party alliance is demanding an end to utility crises, price hikes, and corruption, with a convoy of around 1,500 vehicles.
details: The Jamaat-e-Islami led 11-party alliance began a long march from Dhaka's Shapla Chattar to Chattogram today, demanding the establishment of people's rights.
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman stated the movement is on behalf of 180 million people suffering from gas, electricity, and water crises despite paying their bills.
The alliance's six-point demands include implementing the referendum verdict, trial of the 2024 July massacre, curbing price hikes of essentials, and ending corruption and extortion.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam warned that if the government obstructs the march, the alliance's six-point demand will turn into a single-point demand.
The convoy, consisting of approximately 1,500 vehicles, is scheduled to end at Laldighi Maidan in Chattogram, with several roadside rallies planned along the way.
To minimize public inconvenience, the alliance coordinated with police and planned to use only one side of the highway to allow regular traffic to flow.
Further long marches are planned from Dhaka to Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 10, and Sylhet on October 24, concluding with a grand rally in Dhaka on November 14.
caption:
From Dhaka to Chattogram: A massive 11-party alliance long march begins to demand an end to utility crises and corruption.

The Jamaat-e-Islami led 11-party alliance began a long march from Dhaka's Shapla Chattar to Chattogram today, demanding the establishment of people's rights.

Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman stated the movement is on behalf of 180 million people suffering from gas, electricity, and water crises despite paying their bills.

The alliance's six-point demands include implementing the referendum verdict, trial of the 2024 July massacre, curbing price hikes of essentials, and ending corruption and extortion.

Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam warned that if the government obstructs the march, the alliance's six-point demand will turn into a single-point demand.

The convoy, consisting of approximately 1,500 vehicles, is scheduled to end at Laldighi Maidan in Chattogram, with several roadside rallies planned along the way.

To minimize public inconvenience, the alliance coordinated with police and planned to use only one side of the highway to allow regular traffic to flow.

Further long marches are planned from Dhaka to Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 10, and Sylhet on October 24, concluding with a grand rally in Dhaka on November 14.
